paper.citation: Brooks SG, Dengel DR. Position-specific longitudinal assessment of total and regional body composition in NCAA Division I football players. J Strength Cond Res. 2025;XX(X):000-000.
paper.abstract: DXA body composition was measured at preseason and postseason in 188 male NCAA Division I football players aged 18-23, grouped into nine position groups. Total lean mass decreased across the season in several positions, with losses concentrated in the leg and gynoid regions, while total body mass, fat mass and bone mass were largely unchanged.
paper.tldr: In 188 Division I football players, lean mass fell from preseason to postseason in several position groups, mostly in the legs and gynoid region, so position-specific lower-body lean mass is worth monitoring.
paper.methods: Retrospective analysis of existing DXA scans collected from 2019 to 2023, with one preseason and one postseason scan per player. A two-factor repeated-measures ANOVA tested season and position effects, controlling for playing status, with Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons.
paper.findings: Total lean mass decreased significantly in defensive backs, offensive linemen, punters/kickers, running backs, tight ends and wide receivers, and leg lean mass decreased in most positions. Gynoid lean mass decreased in all positions except quarterbacks, while total fat mass, bone mass and total body mass did not change significantly. Total muscle-to-bone ratio decreased in defensive backs, defensive linemen, tight ends and wide receivers.
paper.limitations: The observational design and lack of nutrition, training and performance data mean the causes of lean mass loss cannot be established. The sample comes from one university over one season per player, with no seniority or eligibility data, and scan time of day could differ between visits.
paper.practicalImplications: Staff can use DXA to track lean mass by position across a season, with lower-body and gynoid lean mass as the main areas to watch. The study does not test whether any change in training or nutrition prevents these losses.
paper.athleteDev: Use these results as a position-level reference for in-season lean mass change, since losses were concentrated in the legs and gynoid region and lower-body strength and lean mass maintenance may warrant emphasis. The study does not show that changing training or nutrition would prevent the losses.
paper.rtp: The study does not inform return to sport. It contains no return-to-play data on injured athletes, so its composition changes should not be used to make return-to-play or clearance decisions.
